title: DR1 offers each species as its common name with the Latin name in brackets — 'African buffalo (Syncerus spp.)'; the frontend offers the bare Latin binomial, so a user who does not read Latin cannot tell the options apart.

finding.frontend: Every species option is labelled with its Latin binomial alone: under Cow (0102) the four choices read Bison bison, Bos spp., Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis; under Horse, Equus caballus; under Cat, Felis catus; under Dog, Canis lupus familiaris; under Fish, Salmo salar. There is no common name anywhere in the option set, because the catalogue does not hold one — each species is a value and a text and the text is the Latin name (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:15-26), rendered straight through as the checkbox label (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/view-model/commodity-groups.js:3-14).
finding.prototype: DR1 labels a species with its common name first and the Latin name in brackets — 'African buffalo (Syncerus spp.)', 'Banteng (Novibos spp)', 'Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)', 'Water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis)' — falling back to the commodity name in front of the Latin name when a species has no common name of its own (app/assets/javascripts/commodity-search.js:11-17). 123 of DR1's 144 species entries carry a commonName next to their label — every one of the 11 under Cattle (app/data/commodities-0102-species.js:3-15), the 3 under Horse and the 106 under Other live mammals, plus Cat, Dog and Ferret. The other 21, spread over the remaining 15 commodities, have none and take the fallback, so a user searching for sheep is offered 'Sheep (Ovis aries)'. The common name is not decoration: it is what DR1's search matches on first, and the search hint tells the user so — 'You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus).' The results panel is ordered by that display label rather than by the Latin name, which is why Cattle opens with African buffalo rather than Bison bison (app/utils/commodity-search-data.js:1-31).
finding.difference: Give every species in the catalogue a common name and render the option label as 'Common name (Latin name)', falling back to 'Commodity name (Latin name)' where a species has no common name. This is presentation plus one extra piece of data per species, so it can be done in the frontend against the current stub before the real catalogue arrives — but it has to be in place before the search control ships, because DR1's search hint promises the user can find a commodity by its common name.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a common name rendered against any species option on the frontend's What are you importing? page.
finding.correction: The finding stands and the difference slot was already right, but one supporting claim was wrong and has been fixed. Claimed 'Every species entry in the catalogue carries a commonName next to its label'. It does not: 21 of DR1's 144 species entries have no commonName — all of Bees, Camel, Chicken, Duck, Goat, Goose, Guinea fowl, Ornamental fish, Ostrich, Parrot, Pig, Rabbit, Reptile, Sheep and Turkey — and those take the 'Commodity name (Latin name)' fallback the finding already describes. Checked against the catalogue JSON the prototype embeds in the page (capture/html/prototype/dr1-what-are-you-importing-results.html, the app-commodity-search__data script) and against app/data/commodities.js. Everything else verified from the rendered DOM on both sides rather than from source: the frontend's eight checkbox labels are the bare binomials Bison bison, Bos spp., Bos taurus, Bubalus bubalis, Equus caballus, Felis catus, Canis lupus familiaris and Salmo salar, and DR1's results rows read 'African buffalo (Syncerus spp.)', 'Banteng (Novibos spp)', 'Bison (Bison spp)', 'Bison bison (Bison bison)' and 'Buffalo (Bubalus spp (including Anoa))', in that display-label order.

relatedTo.why: DR1's search matches on the common name, so the label and the search control depend on the same missing data.
